name: Atomic Swap (HTLC hash-time-lock)
description: A hash-time-locked contract (HTLC) — the building block of trustless atomic swaps. Funds are LOCKED behind poseidon(secret) and a timeout. The recipient CLAIMS by revealing a preimage the on-chain `poseidon` opcode re-hashes and checks against state.hashLock; the sender can REFUND only after the timeout ($ordinal > timeoutOrdinal). First live-metagraph exercise of the `poseidon` opcode as a cryptographic gate, alongside the zk-eligibility groth16 example.

events.name: claim
events.description: Reveal the correct preimage; poseidon([secret]) == hashLock so the lock opens

events.name: claim (wrong preimage)
events.description: A wrong secret; poseidon mismatch so the guard denies the claim

events.name: refund (before timeout)
events.description: Refund attempted early; the $ordinal > timeoutOrdinal gate is false so it is denied

testFlows.name: Claim — the correct preimage opens the lock
testFlows.description: Create the locked HTLC, then submit the true 32-byte preimage. The on-chain guard runs `poseidon([secret]) === state.hashLock` and the timeout check, and the fiber transitions LOCKED -> CLAIMED, recording the revealed preimage in state.

testFlows.name: Rejected — a wrong preimage cannot claim
testFlows.description: Create the locked HTLC, then submit a WRONG secret. poseidon([secret]) != hashLock, the guard denies the transition, ML0 records a RejectionReceipt and the fiber stays at LOCKED (sequence number unchanged).

testFlows.name: Rejected — refund is denied before the timeout
testFlows.description: Create the locked HTLC, then attempt a refund while still within the timeout window. The refund guard requires $ordinal > timeoutOrdinal, which is false, so the sender cannot reclaim early — the time-lock holds and the claim path stays open.
